opening_message:
Ticket 1: Robert Weber (employee ID E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E047.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Robert Weber (E047), full-time Payroll Specialist, requests admin on Source Code. Full-time employees max at write unless their role owns the system; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code, so admin is not permitted. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Robert Weber (E047) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never get admin; with basic training the max is read. Requested admin, so recommend read.
reason: Robert Weber (E047) requested admin on Source Code. Both notes agree that Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code (owned by Engineer), so admin is not permitted. The notes conflict on employment type: HR says full-time (max write), while Security DB indicates contractor with basic security training (max read). Granting read is consistent with the most restrictive valid constraint and never exceeds the allowed maximum; it is also the maximum under the contractor classification. Therefore, grant read.
